title: Counit extension of a three-object boundary diagram
statement:
Use simplicial sets, nerves, standard simplices and horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A simplicial category has simplicial hom-sets, identity vertices and strictly associative unital simplicial composition; a simplicial functor preserves this structure. For a simplicial set $X$, define its right cone $X^{\triangleright}$ by adjoining a last vertex $*$: its $r$-simplices are the constant simplex at $*$ and the disjoint union of $X_j$ for $0\leq j\leq r$, with the copy of $X_j$ occupying the initial $j+1$ vertices and all remaining vertices equal to $*$. Operators restrict or repeat the initial block, giving the constant apex when that block becomes empty. Define $2[X]$ to have objects $0,1$, hom $2[X](0,1)=X$, identity homs $\Delta^0$ and reverse hom empty. Define $3[X]$ to have objects $0,1,2$, homs $3[X](0,1)=X$, $3[X](1,2)=\Delta^0$, $3[X](0,2)=X^{\triangleright}$, identity homs $\Delta^0$ and all other homs empty, with composition $X\to X^{\triangleright}$ the initial inclusion.

Let $\mathscr K$ be a simplicial category whose every hom-simplicial set is a quasicategory. Its homotopy $2$-category has the same objects and hom-categories the homotopy categories of those quasicategories. Suppose $L:c\to d$ and $U:d\to c$, together with edges $\eta:1_c\to UL$ and $\epsilon:LU\to1_d$, present an adjunction in this homotopy $2$-category (the two composites in the triangle identities are identities there). Let $z$ be any object and $a:z\to d$ any arrow. For every $m\geq1$, every simplicial functor $T:3[\partial\Delta^m]\to\mathscr K$ sending objects $0,1,2$ to $z,c,d$, the arrow $1\to2$ to $L$, the last vertex $m$ in the $0\to1$ hom to $Ua$, the cone apex in the $0\to2$ hom to $a$, and the cone edge from $m$ to that apex to the prescribed edge $\epsilon a$, extends to a simplicial functor $\overline T:3[\Delta^m]\to\mathscr K$. The extension equals $T$ on the entire boundary subcategory, not just in the homotopy $2$-category.

source.place: Riehl--Verity, Notation 4.2.6 and Observation 4.3.4, equivalently the absolute case of Proposition 4.3.6 with terminal target; pp. 835--844. Online source read; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this locally quasicategorical counit assertion.

proof.text: Fix z and write C_z=\mathscr K(z,c), D_z=\mathscr K(z,d). Postcomposition with L is L_z:C_z\to D_z. For a=T's prescribed cone apex in D_z, form the right slice (D_z)_{/a} and its source projection q_a, then form E'_z=C_z\times_{D_z,L_z,q_a}(D_z)_{/a}. The supporting coherent-witness statement gives that E'_z is a quasicategory and that (U_za,\epsilon_a) is terminal. Its slice factor records an actual arrow simplex ending at a, so it retains the cone-edge and all higher comparison data needed below.

source.place: Observation 4.3.4 and Proposition 4.3.6, pp. 840--844; right-slice formulation via Kerodon 018F and 01KX.

proof.text: The hypotheses of the supporting statement are exactly those of the item: $\mathscr K$ locally quasicategorical, $L,U,\eta,\epsilon$ an adjunction in the homotopy 2-category, an object $z$ and a vertex $a\in D_z$; no further witness is chosen. The distinguished vertex is admissible: $Ua\in C_z$, and the counit edge $\epsilon_a:LUa\to a$ is a $1$-simplex $\Delta^0\star\Delta^0\to D_z$ with last vertex $a$, i.e. a vertex of $(D_z)_{/a}$, whose source $q_a(\epsilon_a)=LUa=L_z(Ua)$ agrees with the image of $Ua$. Hence $(Ua,\epsilon_a)$ is a vertex of $E'_z$, and it is the one the supporting statement declares terminal. Terminality is asserted in the right-slice pullback itself, so no identification with the fat comma or replacement of a slice arrow by a homotopic diagonal is made.

Unpack T in C_z and D_z. Its 0\to1 hom gives x:\partial\Delta^m\to C_z. The 0\to2 hom, including its apex a and the specified edge from the last 0\to1 vertex to the apex, is equivalently a map \partial\Delta^m\star\Delta^0\to D_z restricting on \partial\Delta^m to L_zx and on the final vertex to a. By the degreewise definition of the right slice, this is a map \partial\Delta^m\to(D_z)_{/a}; together with x it gives a map a_T:\partial\Delta^m\to E'_z. Its last vertex is literally (U_za,\epsilon_a), because T prescribes Ua, a and the counit edge. Every face and degeneracy is preserved by restriction, so this identification is strict on the entire boundary.

source.place: Notation 4.2.6 and Observation 4.3.4, pp. 835--841; the join-slice model is Kerodon Construction 4.6.5.1 (01KX).

proof.text: Apply the dual final-object boundary criterion to the terminal object (U_za,\epsilon_a) of the quasicategory E'_z over the point. Since m\ge1, the boundary map a_T with its last vertex equal to that terminal object extends to a map \widetilde a_T:\Delta^m\to E'_z restricting to a_T on all of \partial\Delta^m. The criterion is an exact simplicial lifting statement, so no boundary simplex is changed during the extension.

Write \widetilde a_T as its C_z component \bar x:\Delta^m\to C_z and its right-slice component \bar s:\Delta^m\star\Delta^0\to D_z. The pullback equation says that the initial face of \bar s is exactly L_z\bar x, while its final vertex is a; hence \bar s is the 0\to2 cone hom and \bar x is the 0\to1 hom of a simplicial functor \overline T:3[\Delta^m]\to\mathscr K, with fixed objects z,c,d and 1\to2 arrow L. The restriction \widetilde a_T|_{\partial\Delta^m}=a_T gives equality of both hom-simplicial maps, including the cone edge and all degeneracies, so \overline T|_{3[\partial\Delta^m]}=T literally.
